findings.message: F1 RESOLVED - operator-local path no longer reachable from any ref; the 4 flagged blobs are confirmed unreachable/dangling, not on the branch
findings.detail_md: `git log -p -S'<local-path> --format=%h -- specs/releases/0.4.7/TASKS.md` (both on feature/0.4.7 and with `--all`) returns zero commits. `git for-each-ref refs/original` is empty (filter-branch's default backup already cleaned). The lone stray ref `refs/tags/backup/pre-rewrite-0.5.0` was checked directly: `git ls-tree -r <tag> --name-only | grep -c specs/releases/0.4.7/TASKS.md` -> 0 - that tag predates 0.4.7 and carries no copy of the leaked file. `git rev-list --objects --all | grep <blob>` finds none of the 4 blobs named in the first-round scan (0d8a0c9b67e4, 397a562cf933, 1621479c7281, 98454099c338); `git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs` DOES list all 4 as unreachable blobs - physically present in the object DB until GC, but not reachable from any ref, so `git push` never transmits them. The push-gate replay over the full range (6cef01f854ee4e3c1178791270c9813fa9947730..adcdb2ad88a5f8ebd4fff77afbb58c1eccd00ea3) exits 0 with no BLOCKED line, versus the first-round replay over 6cef01f8..f23466d0 which printed 4 BLOCKED lines naming these exact blobs.
findings.fix_recommendation: None required for the PR gate. Optional hygiene for the operator: `git gc --prune=now` (or wait out the default 2-week grace period) to purge the now-unreachable blobs from local object storage - cosmetic, not a security requirement, since they are unreachable and unpushable already.

findings.message: FR6 copy-drift heal path (doctor_structural.py::fix_tree5) reviewed under OWASP A01/A05 - path-confusion and symlink-follow both closed by design
findings.detail_md: `_tree5_compare` classifies a scaffolded law-file drift into three outcomes: identical (no issue), `was_shipped` byte-match (WARNING, fixable=True), or copy-drift matching neither source (WARNING, fixable=False, never auto-repaired). `fix_tree5` is only ever invoked on an issue this same validator marked fixable, and even then re-derives the repair target from a closed, hand-enumerated `targets` list keyed by matching `issue.path` against `dst.resolve()` - the issue string never becomes a raw filesystem destination (CWE-73 closed). Before any write: `dst.is_symlink()` is checked and the write skipped if true (CWE-59/61 closed - a projected law file symlinked elsewhere in the tree cannot be used to redirect the heal write off-tree). `was_shipped` is re-verified inside the fixer, not just trusted from the earlier check call, so a TOCTOU window where an operator edits the file between check and fix cannot cause an overwrite of customised content. `atomic_write(..., preserve_mode=True)` is used for the actual write (no partial-write window). No finding raised; documented as reviewed-clean.

findings.fix_recommendation: No fix required for this release. If this surface is ever exposed to untrusted input, add an `is_symlink()` guard before any move/copy, matching the pattern already used in doctor_structural.py::fix_tree5.
